overview_classification.summary_label_zh: 同源类群作用、静态公开值型非交互 NIKE

authentication.mechanism: NIIKE itself is a passive-secure NIKE primitive; authenticated distribution or binding of participant public values is outside the submitted primitive.

roles.key_details: Each participant publishes a long-term full-kernel-representation public value and retains a secret action vector.

pre_distributed_material: Counterparty long-term public value pk, published or distributed before key derivation

forward_secrecy.conditions: The submitted static NIKE construction does not claim forward secrecy for compromise of a participant's long-term secret; later protocols may use NIIKE as a component.

protocol_characteristics.identity_binding: The security definition takes identities as inputs, but the concrete KeyAgr algorithm shown in the specification operates on the peer public value and local secret; authenticated public-key/identity binding is external.

technical_classification.construction_paradigm: Commutative non-interactive key exchange from an oriented ideal-class-group action on supersingular elliptic curves.

underlying_primitives.name: Random oracle H
underlying_primitives.role: Security-game digest/key derivation in the HKR-CKS-l proof

hard_problems.name: Restricted Group Action Computational Diffie-Hellman
hard_problems.role: Computational assumption for NIKE shared-key security

hard_problems.name: Group Action Inversion
hard_problems.role: Equivalent group-action problem used in the security discussion

hard_problems.name: Supersingular isogeny path finding
hard_problems.role: Concrete-security constraint when distinct orientations may share a j-invariant

static_contributions: Participant A computes its class-group action with sk_A on pk_B; participant B computes its class-group action with sk_B on pk_A.
key_schedule.session_key_derivation: ss = j(E_AB) = j(E_BA), serialized as an element of F_p^2; the passive-security proof returns H(ss).

correctness.relationship: The deterministic commuting group actions yield isomorphic curves and identical j-invariants for honestly generated keys.

security_claims.claim: HKR-CKS-l passive NIKE security in the random-oracle model reduces to Restricted Group Action Computational Diffie-Hellman hardness.
security_claims.comparison_scope: Two honestly registered participants; passive NIKE model

security_claims.claim: The deterministic, dummy-free and constant-time group action is claimed to resist broad timing and related side-channel classes at the algorithmic level.
security_claims.comparison_scope: Submitted implementations and stated constant-time control flow

claimed_advantages.claim: No online handshake round trip is required after public values have been published.
Key generation and agreement reuse the same one-dimensional isogeny class-group-action machinery.
The action is deterministic, dummy-free, constant-time and admits tuple-level parallelism and AVX-512 IFMA acceleration.
The core construction supports parameter agility and possible extensions to multiparty/group settings.

limitations_and_constraints.description: The submitted primitive does not itself authenticate published public values or participants.
Static public/secret values are used directly and no forward-secrecy claim for long-term compromise is given for NIIKE itself.
The construction requires large, structured common public parameters including a distinguished oriented curve and full kernel representation.
At NGCC-III the submission uses a much larger characteristic and a modified construction because finding a suitably small smooth p and generating the kernel representation are difficult.
Reported benchmarks use an Intel Core i7-11700F, Ubuntu 24.04, Clang 18.1.3, with hyperthreading/turbo disabled.

review_notes: Participant model used; no initiator/responder message flow was invented.

Specification/header size conflicts are preserved rather than silently reconciled.
Independent review against Algorithms 4-5 and Table 7.1 confirmed the unauthenticated static-public-value NIKE classification, zero online message flow, and the specification-priority key sizes.
